newsitem.title: USA: Duramed wants drug label declared deficient.
newsitem.headline: Duramed wants drug label declared deficient.

text.p: Duramed Pharmaceuticals Inc said Wednesday it has asked the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to declare the labeling deficient on Wyeth Ayerst Laboratories' conjugated estrogens tablets, Premarin.
Duramed said it wants Wyeth, a unit of American Home Products Corp, to be required to list all active ingredients on the Premarin label.
Duramed also said it has asked FDA to withhold approval of any new applications involving Premarin until "the drug is adequately characterized."

Duramed's petition follows a determination in May by the FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research to deny Duramed's application to market a generic form of conjugated estrogens tablets that would have competed directly with Premarin.
Duramed said the FDA panel concluded it could not grant its application because Premarin is not adequately characterized and therefore its active ingredients cannot be definitively identified.
"Until the active ingredients are sufficiently defined, a synthetic generic form of Premarin cannot be approved," Duramed quoted the FDA panel as saying.
